source_columns: cohort, participant_id, wave, jq8a1, jq8a2, jq9a1, jq9a2, jq2a2, jq2a3, jdatjjjj, jdatmm, sp_own_age_sbl, age_at_wave
expression:
local({
  age <- if_else(
    cohort == "HERMES3",
    as.numeric(age_at_wave),
    if_else(jdatmm %in% 1:12 & jdatjjjj >= 2012, (jdatjjjj + jdatmm / 12) - (jq2a3 + jq2a2 / 12), NA_real_)
  )
  birth <- jq2a3 + jq2a2 / 12
  phone <- if_else(jq8a1 %in% 1:12 & jq8a2 < 9999, (jq8a2 + jq8a1 / 12) - birth, NA_real_)
  phone[which(phone < 0 | phone > age)] <- NA
  entry <- as.numeric(sp_own_age_sbl)
  entry[which(entry < 0 | entry > age)] <- NA
  smart <- if_else(jq9a1 %in% 1:12 & jq9a2 < 9999 & jq9a2 > 0, (jq9a2 + jq9a1 / 12) - birth, NA_real_)
  smart[which(smart < 0 | smart > age)] <- NA
  order <- as.numeric(wave == "follow_up")
  any_phone <- if_else(cohort == "HERMES3", entry + 0.5, phone)
  any_carried <- carry_within(any_phone, participant_id, order = order)
  any_carried[which(is.na(any_phone) & (jq8a2 %in% 9999 | any_carried > age))] <- NA
  observed <- coalesce(any_carried, smart)
  carried <- carry_within(observed, participant_id, order = order)
  carried[which(is.na(observed) & (jq8a2 %in% 9999 | carried > age))] <- NA
  carried
})
notes: HERMES 1+2: first mobile phone 'gekauft / geschenkt bekommen' (jq8a1 month, jq8a2 year) minus birth month and year, compatible, asked at both waves and each wave keeps its own report. A wave where that is unanswered or not an age takes the participant's any-phone age from the other wave (48 rows carried), and keeps NA where the wave's code is 9999, no phone (58 rows). Only where no any-phone age can be used, the smartphone date of that wave (jq9a1, jq9a2; 6 rows, 5 participants, partial); the smartphone items are otherwise unused. HERMES 3: sp_own_age_sbl, 'age in years when receiving/buying first smartphone', asked at baseline, + 0.5, smartphone only, so the row is partial. Entries that cannot be the child's age are NA: 3 any-phone (negative or above the age at that wave), 4 smartphone above that age, the smartphone year 0 (jq9a2), 4 month codes outside 1-12, and 17 HERMES 3 rows (9 participants) holding 2015-2022 calendar years. HERMES 3 entries compare with the rounded age before + 0.5.
Only the age at a first own mobile phone or smartphone, which is ownership onset, not first use of a screen; mapped to fam_firstphone_age.

expression:
case_when(
  lvl_school_log == "Private" ~ "Private",
  lvl_school_log %in% c("High", "Medium", "Low") ~ "Public",
  .default = "Unknown"
)
notes: HERMES 3 only. 'Private' level of lvl_school_log (25 baseline, 23 follow-up rows; undocumented in the codebook) = Private, and the canton levels High, Medium and Low = Public: the protocol recruited 'all the public schools and private schools' of the region (PMC13098621). School level recorded at baseline, kept at follow-up because participants stay in lower secondary. Proximate: read from a track variable. HERMES 1+2 = Unknown.

Lower-secondary level recorded once at baseline and kept at follow-up. HERMES 1+2 schoollevel, four levels folded: Gym = Academic, Sek A = Intermediate, Sek B and Sek C = Vocational. HERMES 3 lvl_school_log, levels relative to the canton, in order: High = Academic, Medium = Intermediate, Low (third-highest or lower) = Vocational; the undocumented 'Private' level = Unknown. 52 of 843 HERMES 1+2 participants (6.2%, Foerster et al. 2019 Table 1) were in grade 9 at baseline and had left lower secondary by follow-up, so they carry a lower-secondary track into upper secondary; the grade is not released.
